title: Laceration Repair
references: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf), topic: Local Anesthetic Infiltration
StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf), topic: Surgical Skin Preparation
todo: The whole sequence, and which steps come before which, needs a clinician's check; in particular whether the skin is prepared before or after the anaesthetic, and whether the wound is explored before it is irrigated.
Suture material and size, and the number of sutures, are not stated: the closure steps are placeholders until the suturing mechanic is on the forearm.
No tetanus, allergy or neurovascular assessment is modelled.

steps.title: Prepare the skin
steps.objective: Clean the skin around the wound with the antiseptic swab, wiping outward from the wound.
steps.explanation: Cleaning from the wound outward carries skin flora away from it; wiping back over cleaned skin brings it back.
hints: Aim at the skin beside the wound, not the wound itself.
Lower the swab, wipe outward three times, then lift it away.

commonErrors.feedback: Prepare the skin around the wound. Antiseptic in the wound bed itself harms the tissue.

quiz.question: Which way is the skin around a wound cleaned?

steps.todo: Confirm the antiseptic (chlorhexidine or povidone-iodine) and whether it should be kept out of the wound bed as taught here.

steps.title: Infiltrate local anaesthetic
steps.objective: Infiltrate local anaesthetic through the skin beside the wound edge, drawing back before injecting.
steps.explanation: Anaesthetic placed beside the edge numbs the skin that will be handled and sutured; drawing back first shows whether the needle has entered a vessel.
hints: Aim at the near wound edge.
Angle the needle, advance it, draw back, inject slowly, then withdraw.

commonErrors.feedback: Infiltrate beside the wound edge, through the skin, not into the wound bed.

quiz.question: Why draw back on the plunger before injecting?
options: To check the needle is not in a blood vessel
To make the injection hurt less
quiz.answer: To check the needle is not in a blood vessel

steps.todo: Agent, concentration and volume are not stated; whether to infiltrate through intact skin or the wound edge, and the aspiration teaching, are for review.

steps.title: Irrigate the wound
steps.objective: Flush the wound bed with saline from the irrigation syringe.
steps.explanation: Irrigation washes debris and contamination out of the wound, which lowers the chance of infection more than anything applied to it afterwards.
hints: Point the syringe into the wound, flush twice, then lift away.

commonErrors.feedback: Aim the stream into the wound bed, where the debris is.

steps.todo: Volume and pressure of irrigation are not stated.

steps.title: Explore the wound
steps.objective: Lift the near edge with the toothed forceps and look at the wound bed beneath it.
steps.explanation: Lifting the edge shows the depth of the wound and anything left in it, before it is closed over.
hints: Aim at the near wound edge.
Lower the forceps, close the jaws on the edge, lift it, then let it go.

commonErrors.feedback: Take the edge, not the wound bed: the teeth would tear the bed.

steps.todo: What the exploration should find or rule out (foreign body, deeper injury) is not modelled.

steps.title: Place the first suture
steps.objective: Place a simple interrupted suture at the middle of the wound.
steps.explanation: The first suture at the middle halves the wound, so the rest of the closure lines up.
hints: Aim at the middle of the near edge.

commonErrors.feedback: The needle goes through the wound edge, not the bed.

steps.todo: A click stands in for the suture until the suturing mechanic moves onto the forearm; material and size are not stated.

steps.title: Complete the closure
steps.objective: Close the rest of the wound with interrupted sutures either side of the first.
steps.explanation: Evenly spaced sutures share the tension along the wound, so no one stitch pulls the edges apart.
hints: Aim at the far edge, beside the first suture.
steps.todo: A click stands in for the remaining sutures until the suturing mechanic moves onto the forearm.

steps.title: Cut the suture ends
steps.objective: Trim the suture ends with the suture scissors.
steps.explanation: Ends left long catch on dressings; ends cut too short let the knot unravel.
steps.todo: How long the ends are left is not stated.

steps.title: Dress the wound
steps.objective: Check the closure and lay a dressing over it.
steps.explanation: A dressing keeps the closed wound clean and dry while it heals.
hints: Aim at the skin over the closed wound.
steps.todo: Dressing type and aftercare advice are not modelled.
